title: Runtime Decoder Integration Forensics
head: 9f881414e
main_question: Does NaN/Inf appear in decoded R buffer BEFORE contribution (i.e., in the decode/cache path), or only during/after Y = X @ R?
exact_next_fix: The standalone decoder and harness decode both produce finite output (nan=0, inf=0). The 28BR-B runtime test produced nan=896, inf=896. Root cause is either (A) stale build: the 28BR-B binary was compiled before Phase 28AY decoder fix (Phase 28AY was committed May 23 08:58, fixing spanning trit order), so it ran the pre-fix decoder with the spanning trit bug, OR (B) cache corruption: the cached decoded buffer (owned by prt_decode_cache_entry) is being corrupted after decode but before contribution loop inspection. NEXT: (1) Confirm 28BR-B binary was built with Phase 28AY fix applied. (2) Add cache-line boundary scan in harness to detect if decoded buffer crosses page boundary and gets corrupted by adjacent memory write. (3) Run 28BR-B test C with fresh build after this forensics phase.

findings.key_observation: 28BR-B runtime test produced nan=896,inf=896. Standalone decode of identical .trit file produces nan=0,inf=0. The decoder code is identical and finite in both contexts. Either the 28BR-B binary predates Phase 28AY decoder fix, or something corrupts the cached buffer between decode and contribution loop.
